title: Evaluate Division
notes:
Task: Answer variable-ratio queries from equations of the form a/b=value.
Idea: Build directed weighted edges in both directions and DFS from the query numerator to denominator.
Invariant: The running product equals the ratio from the query's start variable to the current variable along the traversed path.
Edge cases: Unknown variables and disconnected pairs return -1.0; a variable divided by itself returns 1.0 only if it is known.
complexity_reason: Each query may traverse the weighted graph; adjacency lists store both directions of every equation.

title: Evaluate Division
notes:
Task: Evaluate ratio queries using a set of known variable equations.
Idea: Build reciprocal weighted edges and search for a path, multiplying edge ratios along the path.
Invariant: The DFS product is the ratio from the starting variable to the current node.
Edge cases: Missing variables or disconnected nodes produce -1.0; known variables queried against themselves produce 1.0.
complexity_reason: Each query may visit the graph, and reciprocal edges are stored for every equation.

title: Nth Digit
notes:
Task: Find the one-based nth digit in the concatenated positive integers.
Idea: Skip blocks of numbers with equal digit width, then locate the containing number and digit offset.
Invariant: n is the remaining one-based digit position after earlier digit blocks have been removed.
Edge cases: n is positive; the final digit is extracted from the decimal representation of the located number.
complexity_reason: The loop advances through digit lengths logarithmically and only one number string is created.

title: Nth Digit
notes:
Task: Return the digit at position n in the sequence 1234567891011...
Idea: Subtract complete digit-width blocks, then calculate the number and position within the remaining block.
Invariant: n is the one-based offset inside the current block of fixed-width numbers.
Edge cases: The input position is positive; long arithmetic protects the block-size products.
complexity_reason: The digit-length block loop has logarithmically many iterations.

title: Binary Watch
notes:
Task: List all valid clock times with exactly turnedOn LEDs illuminated.
Idea: Enumerate every hour and minute and retain pairs whose combined set-bit count equals turnedOn.
Invariant: Each emitted time has a valid hour/minute range and the requested total number of lit bits.
Edge cases: Hours range from 0 to 11 and minutes from 0 to 59; minutes are formatted with two digits.
time_complexity: O(1) for the fixed clock domain
complexity_reason: Only 720 possible times are enumerated.

title: Binary Watch
notes:
Task: Return every watch time with exactly the requested number of lit LEDs.
Idea: Enumerate all 12×60 valid hour-minute combinations and count set bits.
Invariant: A time is added only if its hour and minute are in range and their combined bit count matches turnedOn.
Edge cases: Minutes are formatted with leading zeros; the fixed search space is small.
time_complexity: O(1) for the fixed clock domain
complexity_reason: Exactly 720 candidate times are checked.

title: Remove K Digits
notes:
Task: Remove k digits to produce the smallest possible nonnegative decimal value.
Idea: Maintain an increasing digit stack and pop larger trailing digits when a smaller digit arrives.
Invariant: The stack is the smallest prefix possible after the deletions made so far.
Edge cases: Remove any remaining digits from the end if k remains; strip leading zeros and return "0" for an empty result.
complexity_reason: Each digit is pushed once and popped at most once.

title: Remove K Digits
notes:
Task: Find the smallest number after removing exactly k digits.
Idea: Use a character stack, removing larger trailing digits when a smaller digit arrives; trim leftover digits from the end.
Invariant: The kept prefix is monotonic as far as possible after the deletions made.
Edge cases: Strip leading zeros and return "0" when no nonzero digit remains.
complexity_reason: Each digit is inserted once and removed at most once.

title: Frog Jump
notes:
Task: Decide whether the frog can reach the final stone with jumps differing from the previous jump by at most one.
Idea: Map each stone position to jump lengths that can land there and propagate k-1, k, and k+1.
Invariant: jumps[pos] contains every positive last-jump length known to reach pos.
Edge cases: The first jump must be one; if the second stone is not at position one, the frog cannot start.
complexity_reason: There can be O(n) reachable jump lengths per stone and each is propagated to three candidate steps.

title: Frog Jump
notes:
Task: Determine whether the frog can reach the last stone under the jump-length rule.
Idea: Store reachable last-jump lengths for each stone and propagate the three legal next lengths.
Invariant: Each set contains jump lengths that can reach its stone position.
Edge cases: The first move is exactly one; stones are unique and sorted.
complexity_reason: Each stone can store up to O(n) distinct jump lengths.

title: Sum of Left Leaves
notes:
Task: Sum values of leaf nodes that are left children of their parents.
Idea: At each node, add the left child's value if it is a leaf; otherwise recurse into both subtrees.
Invariant: The recursive result is the sum of qualifying left leaves in that subtree.
Edge cases: A null root and a single root node contribute zero.
complexity_reason: Every node is visited at most once and recursive depth is tree height.

title: Sum of Left Leaves
notes:
Task: Return the sum of all left-child leaves in a binary tree.
Idea: Check whether the left child is a leaf; add its value if so, otherwise recurse into the child subtrees.
Invariant: Each call returns the qualifying sum for its subtree.
Edge cases: Null trees and trees with no left leaves return zero; TreeNode is judge-provided.
complexity_reason: The recursion visits each node once with stack depth proportional to height.

title: Convert a Number to Hexadecimal
notes:
Task: Convert a signed 32-bit integer to lowercase hexadecimal without built-in conversion.
Idea: Mask to 32 bits, then repeatedly extract the lowest four bits and shift right.
Invariant: Each extracted nibble is the next least-significant hexadecimal digit of the unsigned 32-bit representation.
Edge cases: Negative inputs use two's-complement representation and produce eight hex digits; zero returns "0".
complexity_reason: At most eight hexadecimal nibbles are processed.

title: Convert a Number to Hexadecimal
notes:
Task: Return the lowercase hexadecimal representation of a 32-bit signed integer.
Idea: Repeatedly append the lowest four bits and use unsigned right shift.
Invariant: Each iteration removes one low nibble from the two's-complement bit pattern.
Edge cases: Unsigned shifting handles negative numbers; zero is handled separately.
complexity_reason: A 32-bit integer requires at most eight nibble extractions.

title: Queue Reconstruction by Height
notes:
Task: Reconstruct a queue where each person's k equals the number of preceding people at least as tall.
Idea: Sort people by descending height and ascending k, then insert each person at index k.
Invariant: Before inserting a shorter person, all people already placed are at least as tall, so k directly gives its position.
Edge cases: Equal heights are ordered by ascending k; the input is rearranged into the returned queue.
complexity_reason: List insertion may shift O(n) entries for each person.

title: Queue Reconstruction by Height
notes:
Task: Rebuild the queue from height and preceding-taller-person counts.
Idea: Place tallest people first; for each person, insert at index k.
Invariant: All previously inserted people are at least as tall as the current person, making the insertion index satisfy k.
Edge cases: Sort equal heights by increasing k so earlier insertions remain consistent.
complexity_reason: ArrayList insertion shifts elements, producing quadratic worst-case work.

title: Trapping Rain Water II
notes:
Task: Compute trapped rainwater in a 2D height map.
Idea: Seed all boundary cells in a min-heap, then expand inward from the lowest current boundary and raise each neighbor to the effective water level.
Invariant: The heap's height is the lowest known boundary level enclosing unvisited cells.
Edge cases: Grids smaller than 3 rows or columns trap no water; visited prevents processing a cell twice.
complexity_reason: Each cell is inserted into the heap once and each heap operation is logarithmic.

title: Trapping Rain Water II
notes:
Task: Find total water trapped by a 2D elevation map.
Idea: Push all boundary cells into a min-heap and flood toward interior cells from the lowest boundary.
Invariant: The popped effective height is the lowest enclosing boundary known for the cell being expanded.
Edge cases: Small grids trap zero water; each cell is marked visited when enqueued to avoid duplicate processing.
complexity_reason: Each grid cell enters the priority queue once, with logarithmic heap operations.

title: Longest Palindrome
notes:
Task: Compute the longest palindrome length constructible from the input letters.
Idea: Use every even pair of matching characters and optionally one odd-count character as the center.
Invariant: Each pair contributes two characters to the palindrome; at most one leftover character can occupy the center.
Edge cases: Empty input returns zero; a string with all identical letters uses all its characters.
complexity_reason: The string is counted once and the map stores distinct characters.

title: Longest Palindrome
notes:
Task: Return the maximum palindrome length that can be assembled from s.
Idea: Add the largest even count for each character and reserve one center position if any count is odd.
Invariant: The accumulated length contains only matched character pairs until the optional center is added.
Edge cases: If any character count is odd, exactly one odd center can be used; all other odd counts contribute their paired portion only.
complexity_reason: The input is scanned once and a fixed-size character count array is used.
